svg.title: How a game and nativeshvc fit together
svg.text: nativeshvc: a native engine for decompiled SNES games
The game, in its own project: its C, converted to call the API directly

g.text: nshvc_game: init, update(input) at update_hz, draw(between) once per picture, shutdown
music code, run on the audio thread · shaders (*.shade) · packaged data · icon
its own chip logic, drawn as draw lists · jobs for its own parallel work
No bridge: no registers or addresses are translated. Built and packaged for each platform by tools/nshvc-build.

svg.text: the game calls nshvc_* (game, audio and job threads)
the engine owns the loop and calls the game
The API · nshvc/nshvc.h · version 6.1 · docs/api.md · the SNES's units, without its limits

g.text: Loop and threads
loop.c, jobs.c
system, game, render, audio,
job pool; state from input only
Picture
picture.c: objects as textures
compose.c: the picture as
the renderer's passes and draws
Sound
sound.c, src/dsp
voices, envelopes, echo,
32,040 Hz, game's music code
Input, files, inspection
input.c: devices as they are
files.c: saves, packaged data
inspect.c, profiling

svg.text: The picture, drawn natively on the GPU at the window's own resolution

g.text: Overlays
the game's UI, in window pixels, margins too
Sprites
instanced quads; the first to show a pixel keeps it
BG1 to BG4, ordered by the mode
tile layers: 8 x 8 instances · image: a quad · Mode 7: a plane
Draw lists, in a layer's place
the game's triangles, lines, images and shaders
Backdrop
palette colour 0, behind everything
On every layer, where its colour is written:
priorities as depth · windows as stencil bits
changes by line as strips of rows
colour maths against the sub screen, then brightness
mosaic, hires, interlace, direct colour, offset-per-tile
texels sharp; edges smoothed by 8 samples a pixel, else 4
Game thread: draw(between) sets it all
only texels that changed are uploaded
Render thread: compose.c makes a frame
its passes, draws, words and uniforms
Passes
sub screen target, only when the maths need it
side targets for draw lists with fewer samples
main: multisampled, depth and stencil, window size,
resolved into the window with margins and overlays
Renderer · src/render · rr.h
Metal · Vulkan · Direct3D 12; knows no console
The window
the picture's shape: 4:3 by default, or the
game's (8:7, fill), centred in black margins
window, events, input devices, audio out, files and threads, for each platform
macOS, iOS, Android, Windows (Vulkan or Direct3D 12), Linux, headless
A new platform implements host.h, and rr.h if it needs a new GPU API. Nothing else changes.

svg.text: Checks live in tests/ and tools/nshvc-check, outside the engine. No emulation runs in the engine.
